10.5281/zenodo.23533323.title: Why Cold Energy Settles: A Tethered Medium Whose Displacement Is the Gravitational Polarization (Working Note)
10.5281/zenodo.23533323.desc: Working note, version 1.2 (2026-10-21; v1.1 and v1.0 2026-10-20; drafted 2026-10-14). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed. kappa = 1/2 is fitted; the theory is not closed.Correction (v1.1; wording fixed in v1.2): the exact static solution needs negative cold-energy density in a thin pancake through the saddle between two bodies (-89 times the mean cold density at R = 0.2 d for a Milky-Way-M31-like pair, -33 for a cluster pair, canonical footing). A medium of positive mass cannot supply this, so near field null points the cold energy must depart from the law. The total column through the saddle is still positive (negative part -0.206, net +0.016 in the solution's units), so neither picture predicts negative convergence there. Prediction: no saddle dip. Under the law the column through the saddle drops almost to zero in a narrow band; a positive medium cannot dig the part below zero density, a missing depth of 1.9 to 2.1 Msun/pc^2 (Milky-Way-M31-like pair) and 4.6 to 5.1 Msun/pc^2 (cluster pair). Published stacked lensing of luminous-red-galaxy pairs (arXiv:1702.08485) cannot test this yet (S/N below 1; about twelve times as many pairs needed). v1.1 called this "no negative lensing trough"; that wording was imprecise. The numbers are unchanged.Galaxy rotation curves follow one relation between observed and baryonic acceleration, and in this framework its scale is set by dark energy, a0 = (1/2) c sqrt(G rho_DE). Clusters and the cosmic web also need a cold, collisionless mass component, 'cold energy', with Omega_c/Omega_b = 5.364 (measured). This short note explains why that component arranges itself, galaxy by galaxy, into exactly the profile the relation demands.Cold energy is treated as a medium of real rest mass whose displacement P is the gravitational polarization. With K = 4 pi G and u = K|P|, the action is L = -|grad Phi - K P|^2/(2K) - rho_b Phi - W_rem(u) - (gamma/2)|grad P|^2, with K dW_rem/du = u^2/(a0 - u) and gamma = K L*^2/2. Varying Phi gives the baryons' Newtonian flux; varying P balances the baryons' inward pull g_N against the vacuum's push-back u^2/(a0 - u). The unique rest state is g_N = g^2/(g + a0), the simple interpolating function.The stiffness length L* lies between 24 pc (set by Newtonian outer-halo globular clusters) and about 1 kpc. It screens the Solar System: Cassini's quadrupole is at most 5e-8 of the 2026 bound and the only residue is a uniform sunward pull of at most 2.4e-16 m/s^2. With catchment supply and condensed-only sourcing, the framework's own 1024^3 simulations are consistent with raw KiDS-1000 cosmic shear on both footings (Delta chi^2 -7.70 and -7.18 against a same-pipeline control) with inherited initial conditions; rerun with the framework's own initial conditions, the canonical footing still passes (Delta chi^2 -10.08), while the alternative-footing rerun is queued. An earlier own-supply rule is excluded by isolated-galaxy lensing, and an expelled-gas rule for hot-gas systems fails on the full 318 eRASS1 clusters.Not derived: kappa = 1/2, Omega_c/Omega_b, L*, why only condensed baryons tether, and the relativistic completion. Sealed kill lines: a Cavendish test at four times the source acceleration (|dG/G| < 1e-6), a probe beyond 1000 AU (no non-thermal anomaly at or above 1e-13 m/s^2), and Gaia DR4 wide binaries (Newtonian). AI assistance: Anthropic's Claude, with review by parallel AI sessions.

10.5281/zenodo.23532885.title: What a Dark-Energy-Tied Galaxy Law Demands of Its Cold Sector: No-Go Theorems, a Covariant Parent, and the Labelled-Domain Construction (Working Note)
10.5281/zenodo.23532885.desc: Working note, version 1.0 (2026-10-21). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed. kappa = 1/2 is fitted; the theory is not closed.Structural lanes (criteria frozen before computing, mutation controls, post-hoc amendments disclosed, both a0 footings reported and never pooled) asking what any consistent theory of the collisionless 'cold energy' medium of a gravity framework must look like. The framework's galactic law is g_N = g^2/(g + a0), a0 = (1/2) c sqrt(G rho_DE); its extra gravitating mass is the cold energy, not a particle.(1) A covariant parent: a fluid effective theory of comoving labels contains the record's static field equation under five stated conditions (CONDITIONAL). It reproduces the law to 2.2e-16 and has an isotropic dust background, a derived field-aligned stress, linear well-posedness and slip <= 1.54e-5. The medium's identity div P = rho - rhobar holds exactly through shell crossing, so the record's postulate that freed cold energy stays free cannot be derived from it. (2) No-go results: if the medium's excess is the law's phantom, the deep law forces the tether to cancel the medium's own gravity (no linear self-gravity, no gravity between tethered components). No ghost-free local Lagrangian switches the tether off in the linear universe without a vacuum offset 15-25 times the slip bound. A local second-order field that supplies the deep law must carry an external-field effect. Every tether without membership labels makes a satellite's medium hover while its stars fall. (3) No causal non-local parent has the record's cosmological engine as its exact limit: the engine's source relocation cannot conserve momentum, its resolution cut switches the law off for 128 of 175 SPARC galaxies, and its phantom is a global QUMOND field with an external-field effect. (4) Energy: the record's settling does not conserve energy, and no energy-conserving repair that keeps the released energy inside matter brings an infalling halo onto the law. (5) The labelled-domain construction removes the satellite hover and the linear-growth flag, but closes energy only through a non-dynamical label energy (NOT CONSISTENT AS SPECIFIED under its frozen rule; CONDITIONAL only under a post-hoc amendment), and it overshoots the eRASS1 cluster outer shear (Z = -9.3 canonical, -11.9 alternative). No complete parent survives. The two-footing shear pass of the companion notes remains a computational result of an engine whose physical parent is not established. (6) Data: faint gas-rich rotators do not reach the dwarfs' accelerations (not diagnostic); Coma ultra-diffuse galaxies sit above the derived ceiling, but not at 3 sigma once systematics are included; clusters modelled as untethered cold energy match the shear stack at the primary corner only, a fragile match.Not derived: kappa = 1/2, the cold-to-baryon supply ratio, the retained fraction, the stiffness length. Companion notes: PAPER55 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23482936) and PAPER56. AI assistance: Anthropic's Claude (analysis lanes, review, drafting).

10.5281/zenodo.23251231.title: Dark Energy as the Vacuum Energy of the MOND Field: a Consistent Model with a Turn-Off Near 1e-8 m/s^2
10.5281/zenodo.23251231.desc: Version 1.2 (corrections from an independent claim-by-claim audit: the band quoted as 2 sigma was the 1 sigma band, since Lambda/a0^2 scales as a0^-2; the a0 attributions; the Upsilon-free turn-off fit; the RAR-kernel vacuum value; the zero-point wording. AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed). We propose that the observed dark energy is the vacuum (zero-field) energy of the field that produces MOND. In QUMOND and the nonrelativistic limit of bimetric MOND this energy is Lambda c^4/a0^2 = (1/2) int (nu - 1) d(y^2), identical in both bimetric classes and automatically de Sitter. The quadrature kernel sqrt(1 + 1/y) makes it diverge and violates the planetary ephemerides; one strong-field turn-off cures both and gives Lambda c^4/a0^2 ~ (pi/4) y_t. With measured a0 = 1.097e-10 m/s^2 the observed Lambda fixes y_t = 94 (74-120 at 1 sigma, 58-153 at 2 sigma), a turn-off near 1.0e-8 m/s^2, allowed by SPARC and every inner planet. Predictions: w = -1 with a time-constant a0 (or a0 proportional to sqrt(rho_DE) if dark energy evolves); a MOND turn-off near 1e-8 m/s^2 (a signature of at most ~0.002 dex, beyond any galaxy-scale probe); Lambda as field energy rather than a zero-point sum (any matter vacuum energy must still be cancelled). The Lambda match needs the quadrature kernel with a turn-off: with the RAR kernel the integral converges to 12.99, 5.6 times below the observed 73.19. The coefficient a0 = (1/2) c sqrt(G rho_Lambda) is NOT derived: a Lean proof shows it is independent of the other ingredients, and the turn-off scale is a new constant. The cold mass of cosmology is still required.

10.5281/zenodo.23171085.title: A Strong-Field Turn-Off for the Quadrature MOND Kernel: Planetary Safety, a Finite Vacuum Term, and the Offset Reading
10.5281/zenodo.23171085.desc: Version 1.0 (AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed). The quadrature law g^2 = g_N^2 + a0 g_N (nu = sqrt(1 + 1/y), Milgrom 1999 eq 9) has a slow strong-field tail, nu - 1 ~ 1/(2y): held to all accelerations it gives a constant a0/2 anomaly in the Solar System, 1279 times the Earth-Mars ephemeris bound, and it makes the vacuum term of the theory's field Lagrangian (QUMOND, bimetric MOND) diverge. We replace the tail by nu_fix = 1 + (sqrt(1 + 1/y) - 1)/(1 + (y/y_t)^2). On SPARC it is indistinguishable from the exact law for y_t >= 100 (|Delta chi2| <= 1.06); a direct fit bounds y_t only from below; every planet passes for y_t <= 7.7e5; the vacuum term becomes finite, Lambda/a0^2 ~ (pi/4) y_t. Under the offset reading (the a0 sector's vacuum energy is the dark energy, an input) y_t = 128.9 on the kappa = 1/2 footing and 94-103 for measured a0. The value is shape-dependent and does not derive kappa = 1/2, which stays fitted.

10.5281/zenodo.23397365.title: A Two-Configuration Cavendish Test That Separates Low-Acceleration Gravity Models: A Proposal for G Metrology Groups (Working Note)
10.5281/zenodo.23397365.desc: Working note, version 1.0 (2026-10-15). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed.We propose an inexpensive laboratory measurement that sharply separates low-acceleration gravity models: the fractional change delta in the measured G when the source masses' acceleration at the test masses is changed by a factor of four on the same torsion-balance apparatus. A source-field-boost model (Klein's interpolation as used by Scarpa, Falomo and Treves 2026) predicts about 340 ppm between half and twice the Quinn et al. source acceleration; a dark-energy-tied framework screened at laboratory scales predicts |delta| below 1e-6 (model value of order 1e-20); Newtonian gravity predicts zero. Separating the boost prediction needs about 30-50 ppm on the difference, within reach of leading G metrology groups. We describe configurations (source density swap preferred; distance change; combined), interleaved and blinded measurement, null checks, a precision budget, and the interpretation of each outcome. Caveat: the Quinn geometry and Scarpa et al. numbers are approximate; groups should recompute predictions for their own apparatus. AI assistance: Anthropic's Claude.
